stem: In the adjoining figure circle with centre D touches the sides of \(\angle ACB\) at A and B. If \(\angle ACB = 52^\circ\), find measure of \(\angle ADB\).
solution:
The sum of all angles of a quadrilateral is \(360^\circ\).

\(\therefore \angle ACB + \angle CAD + \angle CBD + \angle ADB = 360^\circ\)

\(\therefore 52^\circ + 90^\circ + 90^\circ + \angle ADB = 360^\circ\) ............ Tangent theorem

\(\therefore \angle ADB + 232^\circ = 360^\circ\)

\(\therefore \angle ADB = 360^\circ - 232^\circ = 128^\circ\)
note: Book's first worked example under the 'Solved Examples' banner on printed p.53; it is labelled 'Ex. (1)' while its sibling on p.54 is labelled 'Eg. (2)' — the book is inconsistent about the label, not about the numbering.

stem: Point O is the centre of a circle. Line \(a\) and line \(b\) are parallel tangents to the circle at P and Q. Prove that segment PQ is a diameter of the circle.
solution:
Draw a line \(c\) through O which is parallel to line \(a\). Draw radii OQ and OP.

Now, \(\angle OPT = 90^\circ\) ..... Tangent theorem

\(\therefore \angle SOP = 90^\circ\) ... Int. angle property ... (I)

line \(a \parallel\) line \(c\) ..... construction

line \(a \parallel\) line \(b\) ..... given

\(\therefore\) line \(b \parallel\) line \(c\)

\(\therefore \angle SOQ = 90^\circ\) ... Int. angle property ...(II)

\(\therefore\) From (I) and (II),

\(\angle SOP + \angle SOQ = 90^\circ + 90^\circ = 180^\circ\)

\(\therefore\) ray OP and ray OQ are opposite rays.

\(\therefore\) P, O, Q are collinear points.

\(\therefore\) seg PQ is a diameter of the circle.
note: In the book's figure 3.18 the auxiliary line \(c\) meets line \(a\) at T and line \(b\) at R, and S is the point where line \(c\) crosses to the right of O; the printed solution names T and S without introducing them in the statement.
